findings.question: q-trigonometry-laws-of-sines-and-cosines-0020
findings.quote: This swaps the two sides, giving $\sin R=\dfrac{10}{7\sin30^\circ}$, which is greater than $1$. The swap looks fine because both lengths appear. Check that each side is paired with its opposite angle.
findings.problem: The round-1 wrong-note finding is not fully resolved. Swapping the side-angle pairs gives sin R = 7 sin 30 degrees / 10 = 0.35, which does not support choosing Zero. The displayed expression instead comes from dividing by sin 30 degrees rather than multiplying by it, so the note names the wrong mistake.
findings.fix: Describe dividing by sine instead of multiplying, explain why moving the sine factor to the denominator looks tempting, and advise cross-multiplying the matched proportion.
